newsitem.title: USA: KCS settles litigation, sees 97/98 EPS hurt.
newsitem.headline: KCS settles litigation, sees 97/98 EPS hurt.

text.p: KCS Energy Inc said Tuesday that 1997 and 1998 earnings will suffer from a settlement with Tennessee Gas Pipeline Co that calls for the companies to end their contract two years ahead of schedule.
The settlement ends litigation in which Tennessee Gas accused KCS of improperly enriching the gas it delivered by adding propane.

The contract, which was to extend until 1999, will end in January 1997 as part of the settlement, KCS said. It would have represented less than a third of KCS's 1997 earnings and less than 20 pct of of the year's cash flow, said KCS Chief Financial Officer Henry Jurand.
Earlier this year a jury in Zapata County, Texas, awarded Tennessee Gas $143 milion for its claims.
Jurand said KCS Energy shares fell from around 40 before the verdict to around 30.

Although ending the contract will lower earnings for 1997 and 1998, cash flow should increase next year because of higher gas prices and accretion from the planned acquisition of InterCoast Oil and Gas Co, Jurand said.
"We think this is going to be very positive in our future direction. We're moving this cloud that has hung over us," Jurand said.
Tennessee Gas was a division of Tenneco Inc until Tenneco sold the division to El Paso Energy Corp.
